question: Which additional mathematical assumptions enter when an exact finite Fourier-mode wave on the cylinder is promoted to a completed energy solution, a weak or distributional spacetime solution, and finally a causal Green operator?
answer: The finite Laurent and named-tail rungs remain exact. The L2 target is now closed for one explicit second-order-arithmetic representation: mean-zero rational polygonal chiral pairs, completed by fast Cauchy names with prescribed rates. RCA_0 suffices to extend exact rational translations to a unique real-time isometric energy evolution. This does not close L3: a coded localized test class and weak spacetime equation remain to be formalized, and causal Green support remains separate.

model.spacetime: R x S^1 with formal time Laurent variable z and spatial Laurent variable w
model.energy_encoding: integer mode weights and squared Gaussian-rational amplitudes
model.explicit_infinite_datum: c_n=1/n^2 for n>=1, whose energy summand is 1/n^2
model.explicit_tail_modulus: N(k)=2^k gives energy tail at most 2^{-k} by telescoping
model.localization_obstruction: The Dirichlet kernel sum_{n=-N}^N exp(inx) equals (-1)^N at x=pi; a spectrally truncated point source is therefore nonzero at the antipode for every N.

adds: coded Cauchy completion with prescribed rate
primitive-recursive diagonal for named real times

ladder.object: An energy solution tested against finite Fourier sequences
ladder.separation: This coefficient-weak notion avoids claiming a spacetime distribution or localized support.
ladder.source_boundary: L2 supplies a completed evolution name, but the present certificate does not formalize test-function integration.

ladder.object: A distribution on R x S^1 tested against localized smooth functions
ladder.boundary: Neither finite Laurent algebra nor a Hilbert coefficient sequence supplies this automatically.

ladder.object: Advanced and retarded solution maps with finite propagation and uniqueness
ladder.boundary: The imported biwave result is conditional and its weakest base and Choice strength remain open.

edges.meaning: Resolving finitely many Fourier modes is enough to construct the exact finite Laurent-wave fixture.
A usable cutoff rule supplies a tail modulus only because that quantitative rule is part of the chosen representation.
A prescribed fast Cauchy rate and finite-code time moduli support the explicit diagonal extension in RCA_0.
Finite total energy alone does not supply a rate of tail convergence; deriving one uniformly remains an open bridge.
The completed evolution name has been constructed, but verifying the wave identity against the declared finite test class remains open.
An identity on finite Fourier tests has not yet been extended to a localized spacetime test-function class.
Finite spectral projection is globally nonzero, so this route cannot certify causal support.
A spacetime distribution alone is not enough: energy uniqueness and support propagation are additional requirements.
Finite propagation is the physical requirement, but an explicit theorem must still construct advanced and retarded maps with controlled support.
Computability changes with topology, regularity, and representation; the two literature results are not contradictory.

literature_dependencies.citation: Klaus Weihrauch and Ning Zhong, Is wave propagation computable or can wave computers beat the Turing machine?, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 85 (2002), 312-332.
literature_dependencies.retrieval_note: The authoritative Cambridge record and article text were reviewed on 2026-08-12, but the direct PDF endpoint returned an HTML redirect in the receipt environment; no content hash is claimed.
literature_dependencies.supported_statement: The paper proves computability of the wave propagator for specified continuously differentiable and Sobolev representations, with a loss of one derivative in the former setting and no loss in the stated Sobolev setting.
literature_dependencies.boundary: This is TTE computable analysis, not a reverse-mathematical RCA_0/WKL_0/ACA_0 classification and not specifically the cylinder fixture.

literature_dependencies.citation: Marian B. Pour-El and J. Ian Richards, The wave equation with computable initial data such that its unique solution is not computable, Advances in Mathematics 39 (1981), 215-239.
literature_dependencies.supported_statement: Under the paper's representations, computable initial data can evolve to a unique wave solution with noncomputable values.
literature_dependencies.boundary: The result is representation-sensitive and is not a no-go theorem for computable Sobolev wave propagation or for the explicit coefficient carrier used here.
